The major problems with paid mods:

  1. No guarantee that the mod will work with your configuration of the game
  2. No guarantee that the mod will be updated in the future
  3. No guarantee of a minimum level of quality
  4. No guarantee that the mod will always work (future updates to the game might break it)

I don't mind paying for extra content for a game, but if it's produced by some random person online I won't. The only extra content that I'll pay for is that produced and guaranteed by the game publisher. Anything else is a nightmare of compatibility and wasted money.

This is an issue that I'm hugely torn on.

On the one hand, having absolutely no effective way of paying someone for their work seems insane to me (don't even bring up the "Donate" button. It may as well be a joke). On the other hand, there are many issues that are a major concern...many of which, were clearly displayed that Valve wasn't ready to present the answers to, when they tried to roll this out last time. How will curation and regulation be handled and what is the screening process? Or, is this more like Greenlight or Early Access, where people are free to throw up any old wank? How much of a launch library exist on launch of this for whatever game it happens to be for? How will compatibility be handled between mods? How will situations of X mod requiring Y mod to run Z mod be handled? Will the Steam refund policy going to be officially extended to mods as well? This list is quite long...I wonder how many questions on it will be answered whenever this comes around.

Hopefully, this time, Valve will, at a bare minimum, know well enough to not roll this out in a title with a well established mod base.
